title: Non-blocking findings from PR #273's round-2 review (DailyHomeworkForm suggestion-gate fix)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's round-2 review of PR #273 (frontend-daily-homework-page-followups-followups's fix that gates useYesterdayTradingSuggestion on `todayQuery.isSuccess && !existingEntry` and adds HomeworkQuestionsForm's render-time suggestedScore adjustment), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. The review's blocking checks (correctness via a real browser walkthrough of all three scenarios, full backend+frontend coverage, static analysis, `make e2e`) all passed -- these are quality/design observations only.

checklist.step: `HomeworkQuestionsForm`'s new render-time state adjustment (`prevSuggestedScore`/`hasEditedYesterdayScore`/the `if (suggestedScore !== prevSuggestedScore) { ... }` block in `DailyHomeworkForm.tsx`) hand-rolls the same 'compare a prop to its previously-seen value, adjust state during render' shape that `useResetOnSubjectChange` (`frontend/src/features/portfolio/hooks/useResetOnSubjectChange.ts`) already generalizes -- the new code's own comments cite that hook as prior art but don't reuse or extend it. Consider extracting a small shared hook (or generalizing `useResetOnSubjectChange` itself) so a future fix to this pattern (e.g. a React version change affecting mid-render setState) only needs to land in one place instead of two independently-maintained copies.

The new test `does not overwrite a user's own answer to "yesterday" if the suggestion resolves after they have already changed it themselves` (and similarly the two strengthened pre-existing tests) synchronize on a fixed `await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20))` after manually resolving the mocked suggestion request, instead of a `waitFor`-based poll for the actual expected UI state. Confirmed via `yarn vitest run ... --reporter=verbose` that this specific test genuinely produces React 'An update to DailyHomeworkForm inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)' / 'ForwardRef(FormControl) ... not wrapped in act(...)' warnings (not just a hypothetical concern) -- a real signal that the fixed-timeout synchronization is racing the actual render rather than reliably waiting for it, which is a latent flakiness risk under CI resource contention even though it passes reliably today. Switch these to `waitFor`-based assertions on the expected DOM state instead of a bare timeout.

Gating `useYesterdayTradingSuggestion` on `todayQuery.isSuccess` (this task's fix) sequences `/api/daily-homework/today` and `/api/daily-homework/yesterday-trading-suggestion` for *every* cold load with no existing entry, not just the existing-entry case the fix targets -- confirmed via a live browser network trace: the suggestion request no longer starts until the `/today` response has already landed, versus firing concurrently before this fix. This tradeoff is already documented and accepted in this task's own `decisions` entry (second entry), so it's not a new finding requiring rework -- but it's tracked here as a design point worth reconsidering later, e.g. by having the backend return the suggestion alongside `/today`'s response (or another data-layer composition), which would also let `HomeworkQuestionsForm` go back to capturing `yesterday_trading_score` in its plain `useState` initializer and remove the render-time-adjustment machinery (checklist item 1 above) entirely.

decisions.decision: Generalized `useResetOnSubjectChange` itself (kept in its existing home, `frontend/src/features/portfolio/hooks/useResetOnSubjectChange.ts`) into a new exported `useOnValueChange<T>(value, onChange)` -- same compare-prev-value-during-render shape, but `onChange` receives the new value instead of taking no arguments. `useResetOnSubjectChange(subjectId, onReset)` is now a one-line wrapper (`useOnValueChange(subjectId, onReset)`) preserving its existing `onReset: () => void` call shape for its three existing call sites (`TradeApgarDialog`, `FollowUpReviewDialog`, `ClosePositionDialog`), unchanged. `DailyHomeworkForm.tsx`'s `HomeworkQuestionsForm` now calls `useOnValueChange(suggestedScore, (newSuggestedScore) => { ... })` in place of its hand-rolled `prevSuggestedScore`/`if (suggestedScore !== prevSuggestedScore)` block, deleting that duplicated state variable and comparison entirely.
decisions.rationale: Considered moving the hook to a new shared location (e.g. a `frontend/src/utils/` or a new top-level `hooks/` folder) since it's now used across two features (portfolio and homework) and `docs/architecture/Frontend.md`'s hooks-placement rule ('live under the feature they serve... not in a single catch-all hooks/ folder') is explicitly scoped to API-concern hooks, which this isn't. Rejected introducing a new folder-placement precedent the architecture docs don't already establish, in favor of the smaller, more surgical change explicitly offered as an option by this task's own checklist item ('generalize `useResetOnSubjectChange` itself'): keeping it in place means the diff is scoped to exactly the two files that needed to change (`useResetOnSubjectChange.ts`'s new export, `DailyHomeworkForm.tsx`'s call site), the three existing portfolio call sites are untouched (no import-path churn, verified via a full pass of `TradeApgarDialog.test.tsx`/`FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx`/`ClosePositionDialog.test.tsx`, all 31 passing), and `frontend/src/features/homework/components/DailyHomeworkForm.tsx` importing `useOnValueChange` from `../../portfolio/hooks/useResetOnSubjectChange` is a one-line cross-feature import, not a structural violation of any documented rule. If a third, unrelated feature ever needs this same pattern, that would be the natural trigger to revisit a genuinely shared location -- premature to do so for exactly two call sites. Verified via the full `DailyHomeworkForm.test.tsx` suite (13/13 passing) plus the three portfolio dialog test files (31/31 passing) after the change, `eslint`/`tsc` clean.

decisions.decision: Replaced the three fixed `await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20))` waits in `DailyHomeworkForm.test.tsx` (the two strengthened pre-existing 'falls back to the neutral default' tests, and the new 'does not overwrite a user's own answer' test) with `waitFor(() => expect(queryClient.getQueryState(homeworkKeys.yesterdaySuggestion)?.status).toBe('success' | 'error'))`, using an explicit `queryClient` passed to `renderWithProviders` in each of the three tests (via `createTestQueryClient()`) so the query's own settled status is directly observable from the test, not inferred from a fixed elapsed time.
decisions.rationale: This is the same established pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase for exactly this class of problem -- asserting a UI state that doesn't visibly change once a query settles, so a plain `waitFor` on the DOM text alone would pass trivially without ever actually waiting for the settle to happen (see `SellFlaggedPositionsCard.test.tsx`'s and `StockDetailPage.test.tsx`'s `queryClient.getQueryState(...)?.status` waits). Rejected leaving the tests as-is (a fixed 20ms sleep): confirmed via `yarn vitest run src/features/homework/components/DailyHomeworkForm.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` before this fix that this pattern genuinely produced React 'not wrapped in act(...)' warnings (matching the finding this checklist item recorded), and after the fix the same command produces a clean run with no such warnings and all 13 tests still passing. Also rejected converting these to a bare second `waitFor` on the expected DOM text (with no `queryClient` involved) for the two 'falls back to neutral' tests specifically, since (per this task's own inherited comment in that test) the expected text is identical before and after the suggestion resolves, so that `waitFor` would resolve on its very first synchronous check without ever waiting for the settle -- the same triviality problem the request-count wait was already added to avoid, just moved one step further out.

decisions.decision: Reviewed checklist item 3 (the `todayQuery.isSuccess`-gating tradeoff, sequencing `/today` and the suggestion request for every cold load with no existing entry) and confirmed no code change is warranted here -- this is purely a documentation/tracking item, not a new finding. The tradeoff was already deliberately accepted and fully rationalized in `frontend-daily-homework-page-followups-followups`'s own second `decisions` entry (the `enabled: todayQuery.isSuccess && !existingEntry` gate change), and re-litigating it, or speculatively starting the backend-suggestion-composition work the checklist item itself flags as a possible future direction, is explicitly out of this task's scope per its own checklist wording ('tracked here as a design point worth reconsidering later'). Re-confirmed the tradeoff is still accurate against the current code: `DailyHomeworkForm.tsx`'s `suggestionQuery` is still gated on `enabled: todayQuery.isSuccess && !existingEntry`, unchanged by this task's other two fixes.
decisions.rationale: Marking this checklist item done with this confirming entry (rather than leaving it open indefinitely, or doing speculative backend work) matches CLAUDE.md's guidance that a documentation-only tracking item already resolved as an accepted tradeoff via a prior `decisions` entry should be closed with a fresh confirming entry, not re-litigated or expanded into new scope. No backend or `HomeworkQuestionsForm`-initializer change was made as part of this task.

comments.summary: Verified `useOnValueChange<T>` is a behavior-identical generalization of `useResetOnSubjectChange`'s prior hand-rolled logic: `useResetOnSubjectChange(subjectId, onReset)` now delegates to `useOnValueChange(subjectId, onReset)` with the exact same compare-prev-value-during-render semantics. All three pre-existing call sites (TradeApgarDialog, FollowUpReviewDialog, ClosePositionDialog) are untouched by the diff; their own test suites (31/31) pass unchanged, and a live browser check of ClosePositionDialog switching between AAPL and MSFT confirmed each dialog opens fresh with no stale prior-subject state and no console errors. `DailyHomeworkForm.tsx`'s new `useOnValueChange(suggestedScore, (newSuggestedScore) => {...})` call site is also a faithful port of the prior `prevSuggestedScore`/`if (suggestedScore !== prevSuggestedScore)` block -- confirmed both by diff inspection and a real-browser race-condition test (delayed suggestion response via Playwright route interception, user edits the field first) showing the suggestion never clobbers the user's own answer.

Confirmed via `yarn vitest run src/features/homework/components/DailyHomeworkForm.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` that the three rewritten tests (the two strengthened 'falls back to neutral' tests plus the new 'does not overwrite a user's own answer' test) now pass with zero React act()-warnings, and that the rewrite is not a tautology: each still asserts the real expected DOM text after the `queryClient.getQueryState(...)?.status` wait settles (e.g. the race-condition test still asserts '0 — Poorly', which differs from the mocked suggested value '2 — Well', so the final assertion is a genuine behavioral check, not a no-op).

Checklist item 3 correctly treated as a no-op: re-confirmed `DailyHomeworkForm.tsx`'s `suggestionQuery` is still gated on `enabled: todayQuery.isSuccess && !existingEntry`, unchanged by this PR, and the tradeoff is already fully rationalized in the parent task's own prior `decisions` entry. Closing it with a fresh confirming `decisions` entry (rather than re-litigating or amending the original entry) is the correct move per CLAUDE.md's append-only decisions-log default.

review.notes: Full review performed: backend suite 1203 passed, 100% coverage; frontend suite passing with 99.76%/99.3%/99.78%/99.82% statements/branches/functions/lines coverage (well above the 90% gate); backend ruff+mypy and frontend eslint+tsc+profit-target-wording guard+validate_tasks.py all clean; independent `code-review` skill pass (medium effort) against the PR diff found no issues, including a specific check of the useResetOnSubjectChange/useOnValueChange cross-feature-import placement question (already recorded as a considered-and-rejected alternative in this task's own decisions). Area is frontend/pages (not backend/signals or backend/portfolio, skill is null) so verify-elder-signal wasn't applicable; no new module/dependency/layer was added so a full architecture-review pass wasn't loaded, though the hook-placement question was checked against docs/architecture/Frontend.md §3's hooks rule directly (scoped to API-concern hooks, which useOnValueChange isn't -- a genuinely arguable, non-blocking placement call already reasoned through in the PR's own decisions entry). No backend/API/schema changes, so no openapi.json regeneration was needed. Browser walkthrough covered the Daily Homework page (golden path prefill plus a live route-interception race-condition edge case) and the ClosePositionDialog for two different tickers (AAPL, MSFT) in a real headless Chromium session (no chromium-cli available in this environment, so driven directly via the `playwright` npm package already vendored in frontend/node_modules) -- no console/page errors in either. Did not get a live click-through of TradeApgarDialog/FollowUpReviewDialog specifically (StockDetailPage's live analysis query stalled indefinitely in my ad hoc manual session for reasons unrelated to this diff -- StockDetailPage.tsx/useStockAnalysis are untouched by this PR, and the full persisted e2e suite's own stock-analysis.spec.ts exercises that same page successfully, so this looks like an artifact of my own throwaway script/session rather than an app regression); relied instead on diff-level equivalence (the wrapper is a one-line delegation with an unchanged call signature) plus each dialog's own full unit test suite passing (31/31 total across the three portfolio dialogs). Ran the persisted e2e suite (`make e2e`): 23/23 specs passed. No blocking findings; no non-blocking findings needed tracking as a follow-up task either (nothing survived scrutiny as an actual open item -- see comments above, all of which confirm correctness rather than flag anything to fix later).
